name: Velocet
description: Velocet is a synthetic SNT-interface accelerant that temporarily increases the signal propagation speed across the organic-synthetic boundary in BCI-augmented users. Thought happens faster — not more accurately, but faster — creating a subjective experience of time dilation where the world seems to slow while the user's mind races ahead. Helix markets it to high-frequency analysts and trading-floor operators who need to process data streams in real time.
effects: Subjective time dilation (perceived thought speed 2-3x baseline)
Massively accelerated BCI data processing throughput
Enhanced pattern recognition in fast-moving data streams
Reduced latency between cognition and BCI command execution
side_effects: Severe temporal disorientation post-dose — the world feels crushingly slow for hours afterward
Neural interface overheating risk with extended use
Micro-seizures in users with substandard BCI hardware
Cognitive fragmentation — thoughts accelerate past the user's ability to anchor them, producing racing-thought anxiety
Long-term use associated with SNT degradation at the organic-synthetic interface
cultural_context: Velocet is the Spire's performance drug — the thing that Tier 4 analysts and Tier 5 traders use to stay competitive in markets that move faster than unaugmented human cognition. It requires a high-quality BCI to use safely, which naturally prices out the lower tiers. Street versions called Quicksilver exist, synthesized by gray-market labs and loaded into cheap neural cartridges — these have a dangerous reputation for causing seizures in users with budget-tier BCIs. The drug has created a class of workers who are physically incapable of doing their jobs without it, which suits their employers fine.
story_hooks: A Tier 5 trading firm is quietly dosing its analyst pool with Velocet through the office's atmospheric system — the analysts don't know they're running hot, and their BCI hardware is beginning to fail in ways that could cascade catastrophically during a major market event.

A street version of Velocet has appeared on the Shelf, priced for Tier 1 access — someone is deliberately flooding the low-tier market with a product that destroys cheap BCIs, and the Shelf's already-limited neural infrastructure is beginning to collapse.

A Velocet-addicted analyst experienced a cognitive fragmentation episode during a dose and made a series of decisions that seemed rational at 3x speed but were catastrophically wrong at normal tempo — now the fallout from those decisions is unspooling, and they can't explain their reasoning without admitting what they were on.
